主要内容: Tucson Electric Power Company proposed an Environmental Compliance Adjustor (ECA) mechanism to recover environmental compliance costs, capped at 0.25% of total retail revenue requirement. The Energy Efficiency Resource Plan (EERP) allows TEP to invest in approved energy efficiency programs, with costs recoverable through existing demand-side management surcharge if targets are met. TEP entered into a 2013 Settlement Agreement with Arizona Corporation Commission (ACC) and others regarding its rate case. The agreement requires ACC approval for new rates, with residential bills increasing by less than $3.00/month. Key terms include a non-fuel retail base rate increase of ~$76 million, OCRB of $1.5 billion, FVRB of $2.3 billion, weighted average cost of capital of 7.26%, return on equity of 10.0%, and a Lost Fixed Cost Recovery mechanism (LFCR) to recover non-fuel costs from lost kWh sales due to energy efficiency compliance. The agreement includes modifications to TEP’s Purchased Power and Fuel Adjustment clause (PPFAC).
